principles.name: Objective native deformation
principles.statement: Response is a function of the frozen objective SPD tensor C[q,q0], or its invariants/spectrum, and not of an observer-dependent infinitesimal strain.
principles.math: C -> Q^T C Q implies Phi(Q^T C Q)=Phi(C); isotropy reduces Phi to phi(I1,I2,I3).
principles.reason: Finite-deformation objectivity is fixed by DEFORMATION-001 and excludes E01 as a complete law, while retaining its tangent.

principles.name: Invariant stored energy
principles.statement: The recoverable constitutive sector is generated by a scalar energy on the admissible C-domain.
principles.math: Phi:D_SPD -> R,  S=2 dPhi/dC (up to the frozen stress convention).
principles.reason: A single-valued conservative potential gives objective stress and path-independent recovery; fluid, plastic, damage and purely rate laws fail as complete sectors.

principles.name: Reference equilibrium and normalization
principles.statement: The reference state is a stationary minimum and its arbitrary energy zero is removed.
principles.math: Phi(I)=0, D Phi(I)=0, and Phi(C)>Phi(I) locally for C != I.
principles.reason: Otherwise the frozen reference carries residual constitutive force or is unstable.

principles.name: Differentiable stress response
principles.statement: Energy has enough regularity to define stress and a weak-field tangent on the interior.
principles.math: Phi in C^2(D_int); S=2D_C Phi and A=4D_C^2 Phi.
principles.reason: BALANCE-001 needs stress and the frozen weak-field response needs its linearization; piecewise mechanisms require a smooth admissible branch.

principles.name: Positive weak-field tangent
principles.statement: The Hessian at the reference state is positive on authorized deformation modes and matches the frozen linear response.
principles.math: delta C:A0:delta C > 0 for nonzero admissible delta C; A0=4D^2 Phi(I).
principles.reason: It supplies local stability, finite real acoustic speeds after kinetic closure, and rules out negative-stiffness completion.

principles.name: Admissible-domain stability
principles.statement: The constitutive branch used by the theory remains bounded below and elliptic/stable on its declared domain.
principles.math: inf_D Phi > -infinity; acoustic tensor a_i n_J A_iJkL n_L a_k > 0 on the propagation domain.
principles.reason: A positive reference Hessian alone does not prevent finite-strain loss of ellipticity, as E02 and flexible spectral series demonstrate.

principles.name: Conservative recovery
principles.statement: Removing load returns the state toward the unique reference minimum within the constitutive branch.
principles.math: Closed quasistatic paths satisfy integral S:dC=0; equilibrium minimization selects C=I.
principles.reason: This is the common surviving content of elastic, hyperelastic, barrier and conservative interaction models.

principles.name: Spatial communication
principles.statement: The governing closure must transmit a local constitutive response between neighbouring locations.
principles.math: rho q_tt + delta E/dq=0, with delta E/dq containing Div P, a gradient operator, or a symmetric nonlocal integral.
principles.reason: Pointwise energy alone cannot propagate disturbances. Communication may enter through balance and need not be an intrinsic constitutive length.

principles.name: Weak-field wave support
principles.statement: With the frozen duration/kinetic closure, linearization has real propagating modes in the required channels.
principles.math: rho omega^2 a=Q(n)a, Q positive on required polarizations.
principles.reason: This requires inertia, P05 and P08 jointly; it is not implied by any one of them.

principles.name: Progressive elastic hardening
principles.statement: Incremental resistance increases along specified loading paths.
principles.math: d^2/ds^2 Phi(C(s)) nondecreasing (with a path and tensor stability qualification).
principles.reason: Polynomial, exponential and barrier families can supply it; neo-Hookean, Hencky and harmonic families show it is not required for recovery or waves.

principles.name: Coercive large-deformation growth
principles.statement: Energy grows without bound along every unbounded admissible deformation sequence.
principles.reason: Useful when global confinement is required, but local viable branches and finite-domain barriers need a different boundary statement.

principles.name: Finite extensibility / barrier
principles.statement: Energy diverges at a finite boundary of its open admissible domain.
principles.reason: Gent, inverse-Langevin and chain analogies have it; polynomial and exponential hardening do not.

principles.name: Intrinsic gradient dependence
principles.statement: Energy depends on spatial derivatives of C.
principles.reason: It regularizes short scales and produces dispersion but adds derivative order, boundary data and usually a length scale.

principles.name: Integral nonlocality
principles.statement: A symmetric positive kernel couples separated points.
principles.math: E_nl=1/4 int int Delta C:K(x,y):Delta C dxdy, K=K^T >= 0.
principles.reason: It is a distinct realization of communication; local balance and gradient interaction show it is not universal.

principles.name: Dissipation and rate dependence
principles.statement: A later duration-compatible sector may damp motion without replacing equilibrium energy.
principles.math: D>=0 and d(E+K)/dt=-D under closed boundaries.
principles.reason: Kelvin-Voigt, standard-linear and visco-hyperelastic entries motivate it, but conservative models recover and propagate without it.

principles.name: Extra internal state or preferred structure
principles.statement: Independent directors, fibres, phases, damage, resonators, particles or conformation sectors are not part of the frozen minimal state.
principles.math: Phi(C,z) with independently prescribed/evolved z is outside the authorized state unless z is derived from q or C.
principles.reason: It changes ontology rather than instantiating the frozen constitutive slots.

principles.name: Irreversible complete response
principles.statement: Plastic flow, damage, bond breaking or permanent topology change cannot be the complete constitutive sector.
principles.math: D>0 on a closed cycle or C not returning after unloading contradicts P02/P07.
principles.reason: Such effects may only be separately authorized downstream; they cannot replace conservative recovery.

principles.name: Pure fluid/no shear storage
principles.statement: A complete response with zero static shear modulus cannot realize the required solid-like deformation response.
principles.math: delta^2 Phi[dev(delta C),dev(delta C)]=0 contradicts P05 on required shear modes.
principles.reason: Longitudinal sound alone is not the frozen constitutive target.
